conclusion: The active Lorentz gas provides a framework for studying transport in dissipative dynamical systems and bridges active matter with classical chaotic transport, with possible relevance to hydrodynamic quantum analogs in periodic media.

title: Quantum Algorithm For Evaluating Lyapunov Stability Of non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Mingwu He And Xiao-Ming Zhang
abstract: Stability is a fundamental property of dynamical systems, and Lyapunov theory provides a rigorous link between stability and eigenvalue distribution. By computing eigenvalues, quantum algorithms may offer potential advantages for evaluating the stability of high-dimensional systems under appropriate assumptions regarding data access and quantum resource requirements. In this work, we introduce a quantum algorithm based on the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) to efficiently resolve the complex eigenspectrum of non-Hermitian matrices and determine asymptotic stability. By employing block encoding and QSVT techniques, we implement a polynomial transformation to approximate the singular value threshold problem, enabling the localization of eigenvalues with positive real parts under appropriate requirements regarding block encoding efficiency, matrix conditioning, state overlap, and precision. We validate the method numerically on a one-dimensional non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain with local gain and loss, demonstrating accurate detection of unstable and stable cases, which is consistent with the results obtained by exact diagonalization. These results show that our quantum algorithm is a reliable and powerful tool for stability analysis and spectral characterization of high-dimensional dynamical systems.
tldr: The paper proposes a QSVT-based quantum algorithm to locate eigenvalues with positive real part and assess asymptotic stability of non-Hermitian matrices.
motivation: Lyapunov stability of high-dimensional systems reduces to spectral analysis, where quantum algorithms may offer advantages under suitable data-access and resource assumptions.
method: It combines block encoding with quantum singular value transformation to approximate a singular-value threshold polynomial, resolving the complex eigenspectrum and localizing unstable eigenvalues under conditions on conditioning, state overlap, and precision.
result: Numerical tests on a one-dimensional non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain with local gain and loss correctly identify stable and unstable cases, matching exact diagonalization.
conclusion: The algorithm is a reliable tool for spectral characterization and stability analysis, but its connection to the researcher's quantum information interests is limited and it relies on strong input assumptions.

tldr: A quantum algorithm paper showing that optimized variable-order Trotter product formulas combined with Chebyshev and cardinal-sine interpolation achieve improved cost scaling and depth for estimating observables after Hamiltonian evolution, without extra block-encoding qubits.
motivation: Estimating observables (or amplitudes) after Hamiltonian evolution typically requires either block-encoding/quantum signal processing with many ancilla qubits, or interpolation-based methods whose cost scales superlinearly in the product-formula order, so cheaper and shallower alternatives are desirable.
method: The author composes product formulas with stable Chebyshev interpolation for the evolution and cardinal-sine interpolation to realize the required fractional queries, using an optimized order that varies with the target accuracy and avoiding extra block-encoding qubits.
result: The scheme attains cost scaling and maximum depth of the reported near-linear form (up to doubly logarithmic factors) in the algorithmic and statistical errors, improving on superlinear interpolation-based approaches and reducing qubit overhead relative to quantum signal processing while matching its error scaling.
conclusion: Trotter-based simulation plus sinc/Chebyshev interpolation provides a competitive, qubit-efficient alternative to quantum signal processing for computing observables or amplitudes after fractional-query evolution.

title: Topological Tricritical Ising Universality Class In One Dimension
authors: Hai-Qing Lin And Xue-Jia Yu Sheng Yang
abstract: Quantum critical points can host symmetry-protected topological (SPT) edge modes even when the bulk is gapless, giving rise to symmetry-enriched universality classes beyond the conventional Landau–Ginzburg–Wilson paradigm. Here we show that the tricritical Ising (TCI) critical point—described by a paradigmatic conformal field theory (CFT) with emergent supersymmetry—admits a topologically nontrivial, symmetry-enriched realization, which we term the topological TCI. We construct this critical point in the cluster O’Brien–Fendley (OF) spin chain by applying an SPT entangler to the original OF model. The two realizations therefore share the same bulk TCI CFT. Under open boundary conditions, however, the original model exhibits the free conformal boundary condition, whereas the cluster model exhibits a spontaneously fixed boundary condition: an infinitesimal boundary field can select one of the fixed boundary states, yielding spontaneous boundary magnetization. We further show that symmetry enrichment and boundary renormalization-group flow provide two routes to the spontaneously fixed boundary condition. Whereas the free and spontaneously fixed boundary conditions of the original model can be interconverted by tuning a symmetry-preserving boundary term, no such conversion occurs for the cluster model along the boundary deformations studied here, even in the strong-deformation limit. Although they share the same conventional boundary CFT (BCFT) data, including the boundary operator content and boundary -function, the two realizations of the spontaneously fixed boundary condition are distinguished by different time-reversal charges of the disorder field, which impose different symmetry constraints on the allowed boundary conditions under symmetry-preserving boundary deformations. For the tested symmetry-preserving boundary perturbations that lift the exact twofold degeneracy, the finite-size energy splitting is numerically consistent with exponential decay over accessible system sizes, in stark contrast to the algebraic splitting at the symmetry-enriched Ising critical point of the cluster Ising spin chain. We also find that the topological TCI realization persists along a critical line in a two-parameter phase diagram. These results establish a symmetry-enriched TCI universality class and uncover boundary distinctions invisible to conventional BCFT data.
tldr: The authors construct a symmetry-enriched 'topological tricritical Ising' critical point by applying an SPT entangler to the O'Brien-Fendley spin chain, showing that two realizations sharing the same bulk TCI CFT exhibit qualitatively different boundary conditions.
motivation: Gapless symmetry-protected topological phases and symmetry-enriched critical points go beyond the Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm, but whether the paradigmatic tricritical Ising CFT admits a topologically nontrivial realization with distinct boundary physics was unclear.
method: An SPT entangler (cluster-type unitary) is applied to the original O'Brien-Fendley chain to build a cluster model sharing the same bulk TCI CFT; boundary conditions, boundary RG flows, degeneracy splittings, and a two-parameter phase diagram are analyzed via boundary CFT arguments and numerical (finite-size) diagonalization.
result: The original model realizes the free conformal boundary condition while the cluster model realizes a spontaneously fixed one, distinguished by different time-reversal charges of the disorder field despite identical conventional BCFT data; the splitting decays exponentially rather than algebraically, and the topological TCI persists along a critical line.
conclusion: A symmetry-enriched TCI universality class is established, revealing boundary distinctions invisible to conventional boundary CFT data and highlighting the role of symmetry enrichment and boundary RG flow.

title: Optimal Phase Estimation In The Presence Of Correlated Dephasing
authors: Srijon Ghosh, Arkadiusz Kobus, Stanisław Kurdziałek, And Rafał Demkowicz-Dobrzański
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2251 (2026).

We investigate optimal metrological protocols for phase estimation in the presence of correlated dephasing noise, including spin-squeezed state sensing strategies as well as parallel and adaptive protocols optimized using tensor-network-based numerical methods. The results are benchmarked against fundamental bounds obtained either via the latest quantum comb extension method or an optimized classical simulation method. We find that the spin-squeezed states offer practically optimal performance in the regime where phase fluctuations are positively correlated but can be outperformed by tensor-network-optimized strategies for negatively correlated fluctuations.

.
tldr: The paper studies optimal phase estimation under correlated dephasing using spin-squeezed states and tensor-network-optimized parallel and adaptive protocols, benchmarked against fundamental bounds.
motivation: Quantum metrology protocols must be optimized under realistic correlated noise, but optimal strategies for correlated dephasing are not fully understood beyond standard spin-squeezing approaches.
method: The authors compare spin-squeezed state sensing with tensor-network numerical optimization of parallel and adaptive protocols, and benchmark performance against bounds from the quantum comb extension method and optimized classical simulation.
result: Spin-squeezed states are found to be practically optimal for positively correlated phase fluctuations, while tensor-network-optimized strategies can outperform them for negatively correlated fluctuations.
conclusion: The optimal metrological strategy depends on the correlation structure of dephasing noise, with tensor-network methods revealing advantages beyond spin squeezing in certain regimes.

title: Observing Quantum-classical Correspondence Through Optical Path Integrals
authors: Li-Man Tian, Yunfei Wang, Ying Zhou, Chang Li, Shanchao Zhang, Xuan Dai, Bai-Chuan Long, Hui Yan, Shi-Liang Zhu And Yong-Li Wen
abstract: The quantum–classical correspondence (QCC) describes how quantum systems recover classical behavior in the semiclassical limit. One of the crucial mechanisms to this correspondence is the concept of action, which governs dynamics in both classical mechanics and quantum path integrals. Despite its fundamental importance, experimental access to the action of individual quantum paths remains crucial yet challenging. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a method to measure the action of quantum paths between fixed spacetime points, based on weak-value measurement techniques. By introducing and analyzing the spectrum of the norm of the action gradient, we identify not only single but also multiple stationary-action paths in systems exhibiting complex QCC. Using an optical setup that simulates photon propagation in free space and under an impulsive potential, we reconstruct pathwise actions and observe sharp dips in the spectrum that correspond precisely to classical trajectories. This work provides a framework for directly accessing and analyzing the action, opening new avenues for experimentally exploring the QCC.
tldr: The paper experimentally reconstructs the action of individual quantum paths using weak-value measurements in an optical simulation, revealing stationary-action paths tied to classical trajectories.
motivation: Quantum-classical correspondence relies on the semiclassical limit of path integrals, but direct experimental access to the action of individual quantum paths has remained challenging.
method: The authors use weak-value measurement techniques in an optical setup that simulates photon propagation in free space and under an impulsive potential, then analyze the spectrum of the action-gradient norm.
result: They identify single and multiple stationary-action paths, with sharp dips in the spectrum corresponding precisely to classical trajectories.
conclusion: The work provides an experimental framework for accessing and analyzing pathwise actions, opening new routes to study quantum-classical correspondence.

title: Van Der Waals Superconducting Electronics: Materials, Devices And Circuit Integration
authors: A Di Bernardo And E Scheer
abstract: Van der Waals (vdW) superconductors (SCs)—atomically thin crystalline materials that can be stacked into more complex heterostructures—have opened a promising avenue for superconducting electronics thanks to their properties that are otherwise difficult to obtain in other superconducting materials. These properties include strong resilience to high in-plane magnetic fields, electrostatic tuneability, and non-reciprocal transport rooted in inversion-symmetry breaking and strong spin–orbit coupling. In addition to highlighting the importance of these properties for superconducting electronics, this review gives an overview of the physical mechanisms that govern and influence superconductivity in vdW materials including Ising pairing, band inversion, and proximity effects at SC/ferromagnet interfaces that do not have an equivalent in thin-film systems. This overview then sets the basis to survey the wide range of functionalities enabled by superconducting vdW devices including gate-controlled devices, superconducting diodes, and circuit elements for readout and control of quantum bits. The review concludes with a forward look at wafer-scale growth and deterministic assembly of vdW devices, highlighting concrete pathways that can enable the transition from vdW device prototypes to deployable components for cryogenic electronics and quantum technologies.
tldr: This review surveys van der Waals superconductors and their device/circuit applications for superconducting electronics and cryogenic quantum technologies.
motivation: Atomically thin vdW superconductors offer properties such as high in-plane magnetic-field resilience, electrostatic tunability, and non-reciprocal transport that are attractive for superconducting electronics.
method: The authors review physical mechanisms governing superconductivity in vdW materials, including Ising pairing, band inversion, and superconductor/ferromagnet proximity effects, and survey device functionalities.
result: The review covers gate-controlled vdW superconducting devices, superconducting diodes, and circuit elements for qubit readout and control, and discusses pathways toward wafer-scale growth and deterministic assembly.
conclusion: vdW superconducting electronics could enable deployable cryogenic electronics and quantum technology components, but the work is a materials/device review rather than a contribution aligned with the listed quantum information research directions.

title: Particle Dynamics In Constant Synthetic Non-abelian Fields: I. The Classical Treatment
authors: Subramanya Bhat K N, Amita Das, Bhooshan Paradkar And V Ravishankar
abstract: Yang–Mills (YM) theory has evolved beyond its origins in the strong interaction to become an effective framework for condensed matter, ultracold atomic, and photonic systems, where synthetic non-Abelian gauge fields enable phenomena such as spin transport, the spin-Hall effect, and polarization control. These systems provide access to gauge-field dynamics beyond the reach of high-energy experiments. In all the above mentioned cases, the state of the system evolves in an effective external YM field. Here, we report the results of a classical study (as preparatory for a full quantum study) of particle dynamics in constant gauge fields produced by constant gauge potentials, by focusing on configurations that are experimentally relevant. We show that consequences such as unbounded trajectories in a constant color magnetic field and unusual correlation between charge and color dynamics have a direct bearing on the physical phenomena observed, especially in experiments involving charge and spin transports. More generally, this work also shows how the low energy systems can act as laboratories to probe quintessentially non-Abelian features such as the Wu-Yang ambiguity.
tldr: This work classically studies particle dynamics in constant synthetic non-Abelian Yang–Mills gauge fields relevant to spin- and charge-transport experiments.
motivation: Synthetic non-Abelian gauge fields in condensed-matter, ultracold-atom, and photonic systems provide experimental access to Yang–Mills physics, motivating a controlled classical study before a full quantum treatment.
method: The authors analyze classical particle trajectories and color/charge dynamics in constant gauge potentials producing constant non-Abelian fields, focusing on experimentally relevant configurations.
result: They find effects such as unbounded trajectories in a constant color magnetic field and unusual correlations between charge and color dynamics, with implications for spin and charge transport.
conclusion: The paper argues that low-energy synthetic gauge-field systems can serve as laboratories for quintessentially non-Abelian features such as the Wu–Yang ambiguity.

title: Coupled Propagation Of Acoustic Topological States
authors: Ming-Zhu Li, Lei Shi, Zhe-Yu Ji, Zhaojiang Chen And Ya-Xi Shen
abstract: We theoretically and experimentally investigate the coupled propagation of two pseudospin states in an acoustic topological heterostructure. Within the framework of coupled-mode theory, the heterostructure is mapped onto a two-waveguide model, in which the two pseudospin topological states serve as guiding modes. The propagation constants of the individual topological states and the coupling strength between them are quantitatively extracted from the projected band structures of supercells. When the two topological states are decoupled, acoustic energy remains confined to the excited topological interface. When the two topological states are coupled, acoustic energy undergoes Bloch oscillation between two topological interfaces. Notably, the energy-transfer coefficient of the Bloch oscillation can be tuned by introducing interface detuning. Owing to the frequency dispersion of the coupling strength, the heterostructure can function as a wavelength-selective demultiplexer. This work establishes a generalized coupled-mode framework for the quantitative analysis and flexible manipulation of topological-state coupling, offering new insights into the design of topologically protected acoustic devices with controllable multichannel functionalities.
tldr: A theoretical and experimental study of coupled propagation between two pseudospin acoustic topological states in a topological heterostructure, mapped onto a two-waveguide coupled-mode model exhibiting Bloch oscillations and wavelength-selective demultiplexing.
motivation: Topological acoustic states offer robust energy transport, but quantitative control over the coupling between multiple topological channels remains underexplored, limiting multifunctional device design.
method: The heterostructure is modeled as two coupled waveguides within coupled-mode theory, with propagation constants and inter-state coupling strength extracted from supercell projected band structures; predictions are verified experimentally in an acoustic platform.
result: Decoupled states confine energy to the excited interface, while coupled states produce Bloch oscillations between two topological interfaces whose energy-transfer coefficient is tunable via interface detuning; dispersion of the coupling strength enables demultiplexing.
conclusion: The work provides a generalized coupled-mode framework for analyzing and manipulating topological-state coupling, enabling topologically protected multichannel acoustic devices.

title: Fast Simulations Of X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy For Battery Materials On A Quantum Computer
authors: Stepan Fomichev, Pablo A. M. Casares, Jay Soni, Utkarsh Azad, Alexander Kunitsa, Arne-Christian Voigt, Jonathan E. Mueller, And Juan Miguel Arrazola
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2265 (2026).

X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) is a leading technique for understanding structural changes in advanced battery materials such as lithium-excess cathodes. However, extracting critical information like oxidation states from the experimental spectra requires expensive and time-consuming simulations. Building upon a recent proposal to simulate XAS using quantum computers, this work proposes a highly-optimized implementation of the time-domain algorithm for X-ray absorption. Among a host of improvements to Hamiltonian representation, circuit implementation, and measurement strategies, three optimizations are key to the efficiency of the algorithm. The first is the use of product formulas with the compressed double factorized form of the Hamiltonian. The second is recognizing that for spectroscopy applications, it is sufficient to control the error in the eigenvalues of the (approximate) Hamiltonian being implemented by the product formula, rather than the generic error on the full time evolution operator. Using perturbation theory to estimate this eigenvalue error, we find that significantly fewer Trotter steps are needed than expected from the time evolution error bound. The third is the choice of an optimized distribution of samples that takes advantage of the exponentially decaying Lorentzian kernel. Through constant factor resource estimates, we show that a challenging model Li[MATH]Mn[MATH]O cluster system with 18 spatial orbitals and 22 electrons in the active space can be simulated with 100 logical qubits and less than [MATH] Toffoli gates per circuit. Finally, the algorithm is implemented on a simulator, and the reconstructed spectrum is verified against a classical computational reference. The low cost of our algorithm makes it attractive to use on fault-tolerant quantum devices to accelerate the development and commercialization of high-capacity battery cathodes.

.
tldr: The paper presents an optimized quantum algorithm for time-domain simulations of X-ray absorption spectroscopy in battery materials, with resource estimates for a LiMn2O4 cluster model.
motivation: X-ray absorption spectroscopy is important for understanding battery cathode materials, but extracting oxidation-state information from experimental spectra requires expensive classical simulations.
method: The authors optimize a time-domain XAS simulation algorithm using compressed double-factorized Hamiltonians, product formulas, eigenvalue-error Trotter bounds, and a Lorentzian-tail-aware sampling strategy, then validate the reconstructed spectrum on a simulator against a classical reference.
result: They estimate that an 18-orbital, 22-electron LiMn2O4 cluster can be simulated with 100 logical qubits and fewer than a specified number of Toffoli gates per circuit, and they verify the simulated spectrum against classical computation.
conclusion: The low resource cost makes the algorithm promising for fault-tolerant quantum devices and could accelerate the development of high-capacity battery cathodes.

title: 2d Quantum-path Interference In High-harmonic Generation Driven By Highly-bichromatic Fields
authors: Xiaozhou Zou, Lucie Jurkovičová, Anne Weber, Cong Zhao, Martin Albrecht, Ondřej Finke, Alexandr Vendl, Annika Grenfell, Wojciech Szuba, Jaroslav Nejdl, Eric Constant, Margarita Khokhlova, Emilio Pisanty, Ondřej Hort And Amelle Zaïr
abstract: We experimentally observe a new type of quantum-path interference, in two-dimensions (2D-QPI), in high-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by an orthogonally-polarised highly-bichromatic field. This regime is characterised by a relatively strong orthogonal second-harmonic component beyond the weak perturbation limit, such that the electron dynamics are substantially modified. In this highly-bichromatic regime, we demonstrate that 2D-QPI is encoded in the measured harmonic intensity modulations with respect to the relative phase of the two-colour field. The modulations of the odd-order harmonics show a monomodal behaviour, whereas the even harmonics are modulated in a bimodal structure. Our calculations using the strong-field approximation and saddle-point method disentangle contributions from multiple quantum orbits in this HHG regime, revealing that the dipole response for both odd and even harmonics inherits the dynamic symmetry of the orthogonally-polarised driving field. This new type of 2D-QPI offers a novel route to HHG spectroscopy of attosecond electron dynamics by lifting up the dimensionality of the quantum paths involved in the interference.
tldr: The paper experimentally observes two-dimensional quantum-path interference in high-harmonic generation driven by a highly bichromatic orthogonally polarized field.
motivation: The authors aim to extend quantum-path interference in high-harmonic generation to a two-dimensional regime and use it as a route to attosecond spectroscopy of electron dynamics.
method: They perform high-harmonic generation experiments with an orthogonally polarized two-color field beyond the weak perturbation limit and analyze harmonic intensity modulations versus relative phase, supported by strong-field approximation and saddle-point calculations.
result: Odd harmonics show monomodal phase modulation while even harmonics show bimodal modulation, revealing multiple quantum-orbit contributions and a dynamic symmetry inherited from the driving field.
conclusion: This new 2D quantum-path interference provides a novel spectroscopic route to attosecond electron dynamics by increasing the dimensionality of interfering quantum paths.

title: Grey-body Factors Of Black Holes *
authors: Roman A Konoplya And Alexander Zhidenko
abstract: Grey-body factors describe the frequency-dependent transmission of fields through the effective potential generated by a black hole or another compact object. They convert the idealized thermal spectrum of Hawking radiation into the spectrum measured by an observer, determine absorption and scattering cross sections, and provide real-frequency observables complementary to quasinormal modes. In this review, we present a unified account of grey-body factors in black-hole physics and related systems. We formulate the scattering problem for asymptotically flat, de Sitter, and anti-de Sitter spacetimes, and discuss the connections between transmission coefficients, absorption cross sections, Hawking radiation, and ringdown. We also review methods for their computation and survey recent developments, including the correspondence between grey-body factors and quasinormal modes, their stability under deformations of the effective potential, wormhole transmission and superradiance, and their behaviour in modified theories of gravity. Finally, we discuss the appearance of grey-body factors in gauge/gravity duality, where absorption probabilities in the bulk are related to correlation functions and transport coefficients in the boundary theory.
tldr: Review of grey-body factors for black holes and compact objects, covering transmission through effective potentials, Hawking radiation spectra, absorption cross sections, quasinormal modes, wormholes, superradiance, modified gravity, and gauge/gravity duality.
motivation: Grey-body factors are needed to convert idealized Hawking thermal spectra into observable spectra and to connect scattering and absorption observables with quasinormal modes and holographic correlators.
method: Review and unified formulation of the scattering problem in asymptotically flat, de Sitter, and anti-de Sitter spacetimes, plus a survey of computational methods and recent developments.
result: Collects relations among transmission coefficients, absorption cross sections, Hawking radiation, ringdown, stability under potential deformations, wormhole transmission, superradiance, and AdS/CFT absorption-correlation connections.
conclusion: Provides a broad reference on grey-body physics in black-hole and related gravitational systems, but it is not focused on quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Collective Excitations In Quantum Gravity Condensates
authors: Adrià Delhom And Daniele Oriti Andrea Calcinari
abstract: A central open problem in quantum gravity is to understand how continuum spacetime emerges from quantum-geometric degrees of freedom in a background-independent setting. A many-body perspective suggests that spacetime emerges as a hydrodynamic phase of many atoms of quantum geometry. This idea underlies several approaches to quantum gravity, and it has been explicitly realised in the group field theory formalism. However, quantum fluctuations beyond the mean-field regime remain largely unexplored. We fill this gap by importing Bogolyubov theory to quantum gravity condensates, showing that leading beyond-mean-field effects manifest as collective excitations, in direct analogy with phonons in laboratory Bose–Einstein condensates. We implement the construction in a tractable group field theory model, where condensates of quantum-geometric atoms reproduce nonsingular expanding cosmologies, and derive the leading beyond-mean-field corrections to the emergent Friedmann dynamics. These results identify a new class of quantum-gravity excitations and establish a controlled bridge between microscopic quantum-gravitational dynamics, many-body collective phenomena, and signatures of spacetime emergence.
tldr: The paper applies Bogoliubov theory to group field theory quantum gravity condensates to study beyond-mean-field collective excitations and their corrections to emergent Friedmann cosmology.
motivation: Understanding how continuum spacetime emerges from microscopic quantum-geometric degrees of freedom remains a central open problem in quantum gravity, and beyond-mean-field fluctuations in condensate models are largely unexplored.
method: The authors import Bogoliubov theory into a tractable group field theory condensate model, treating quantum-geometric atoms as a many-body system and deriving leading collective excitation corrections.
result: They identify a new class of quantum-gravity collective excitations analogous to phonons and compute leading beyond-mean-field corrections to the emergent Friedmann dynamics in nonsingular expanding cosmologies.
conclusion: The work establishes a controlled bridge between microscopic quantum-gravitational dynamics, many-body collective phenomena, and signatures of spacetime emergence, though it lies outside the targeted quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems directions.

authors: Pablo Cordero-Alvaradonatalie Kleyeleanor L. P. Castonalejandra Suarez-Arnedoshamitha Shettysophia Zhangtatiana Segurajoel H. SignificancePersistent interleukin-1β signaling sustains pathological myeloid activation and prevents resolution of inflammation in chronic wounds, yet existing interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β)-blocking biologics are short-acting, systemic, and unable to ...
tldr: This paper develops an active immunotherapy targeting IL-1β to restore tissue repair in chronic inflammatory wounds.
motivation: Persistent IL-1β signaling drives pathological myeloid activation and prevents inflammation resolution, while existing IL-1β-blocking biologics are short-acting and systemic.
method: The authors design an active immunotherapy approach against IL-1β and evaluate its ability to modulate myeloid activation and promote tissue repair under chronic inflammation.
result: The immunotherapy restores tissue repair under chronic inflammation, likely by neutralizing persistent IL-1β signaling and reprogramming pathological myeloid responses.
conclusion: Active immunization against IL-1β may offer a durable therapeutic strategy for chronic wounds and other inflammation-associated repair defects.

authors: Gili Scharflara Donvalleah Ben Guralon Ronaschool Of Physics And Astronomy, Tel-Aviv University, Tel-Aviv 69978, Israel

SignificanceA foundational assumption in the physics of ferroelectrics is that electronic polarization and atomic motion share a single energy landscape. We test this directly in real time by independently tracking both degrees of freedom in SnTe under ...
tldr: The paper experimentally probes nonadiabatic dynamics of the ferroelectric soft mode in SnTe by independently tracking electronic polarization and atomic motion in real time.
motivation: A foundational assumption in ferroelectric physics is that electronic polarization and atomic motion share a single energy landscape; the authors test whether this assumption holds dynamically.
method: The authors use real-time tracking of both electronic and atomic degrees of freedom in SnTe to resolve nonadiabatic behavior of the ferroelectric soft mode.
result: The study reveals nonadiabatic dynamics of the soft mode, indicating that electronic polarization and lattice motion can decouple or evolve on distinct timescales beyond the single-landscape picture.
conclusion: These findings challenge the standard adiabatic description of ferroelectrics and highlight the importance of nonadiabatic effects in soft-mode dynamics.

title: Cooling Fast And Slow: Characterizing The Effects Of Vitrification In cryo-EM And The Subsequent Recovery Of Equilibrium Populations

SignificanceCryogenic electron microscopy images biomolecules trapped in vitreous ice. The extent to which the required rapid cooling causes their ensemble to be perturbed from equilibrium is unknown. We use extensive molecular simulations to quantify the ...
tldr: Extensive molecular simulations quantify how the rapid vitrification required for cryo-EM perturbs biomolecular conformational ensembles away from equilibrium and how those populations recover.
motivation: Cryo-EM traps biomolecules in vitreous ice via very fast cooling, but whether and how much this quench distorts the underlying equilibrium structural ensemble is unknown, which complicates interpretation of cryo-EM density maps.
method: Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of biomolecules subject to fast and slow cooling protocols, characterizing the vitrification process and tracking the subsequent relaxation of conformational populations.
result: The authors quantify the degree of non-equilibrium perturbation induced by fast cooling and characterize the timescales over which equilibrium populations are recovered after vitrification.
conclusion: Vitrification can measurably bias observed structural ensembles in cryo-EM, and understanding the recovery of equilibrium populations is needed to correctly interpret cryo-EM data.

title: Higher-order Corrections To The Field Shift In Atomic Systems
authors: Z Harman And C H Keitel V A Yerokhin
abstract: Differences in nuclear charge distributions between isotopes lead to small changes in atomic spectra known as the field shift (FS). While largely proportional to the change in the mean-square nuclear radius, the FS also contains higher-order contributions with different dependencies on nuclear moments. Their knowledge is required in searches for new physics using King plots, since they contribute to deviations from King-plot linearity observed experimentally in recent studies. We present a systematic expansion of the field-shift energies in terms of nuclear parameters and test its validity against direct numerical calculations for H-like ions. We also compute leading- and higher-order field-shift corrections for alkali-like systems from Li-like to Rb-like ions, and find that their ratios are nearly independent of the ionic charge state, agreeing with the corresponding hydrogenic ratios on a sub-percent level. Motivated by these findings, we introduce an approximation in which these ratios are assumed to be independent of the electronic configuration. It is shown that, within this approximation, higher-order field-shift corrections do not induce King-plot nonlinearities. We conclude that only the small contributions beyond this approximation can contribute to the nonlinearities observed experimentally.
tldr: The paper develops higher-order corrections to atomic field shifts and analyzes their impact on King-plot nonlinearities in searches for new physics.
motivation: Field-shift corrections beyond the leading mean-square nuclear radius term are needed to interpret King-plot deviations observed in precision isotope-shift experiments.
method: The authors systematically expand field-shift energies in nuclear parameters and validate the expansion against direct numerical calculations for H-like and alkali-like ions.
result: They find that higher-order field-shift correction ratios are nearly independent of ionic charge state and electronic configuration, implying that within their approximation these corrections do not produce King-plot nonlinearities.
conclusion: Only small contributions beyond the proposed approximation can explain the experimentally observed King-plot nonlinearities, constraining new-physics interpretations.

title: Spatiotemporal Mode-locked Fiber Lasers: Multidimensional Soliton Dynamics Revealed By Real-time Measurement
authors: Yi Zhou, Can Li, Zhuopeng Han, Kun Jin, Bo Ren, Zhenqiang Tang, Tao Wang, Zhiwen He, Jinyong Leng And Pu Zhou
abstract: Spatiotemporal mode-locked multimode fiber lasers have emerged as a promising platform for investigating nonlinear multidimensional physics, with prospective applications ranging from high-energy pulse generation and precise metrology to nonlinear microscopy. The fundamental mechanism governing ultrashort pulse formation in nonlinear multimode resonators, which can be interpreted as multidimensional dissipative solitons (MDSs), lies in spatiotemporal mode-locking (STML), which achieves synchronous locking of both temporal and spatial modes. In this review, the general principles of STML are initially elaborated, with a focus on MDS dynamics under real-time measurement. Subsequently, we summarize the operational principles of versatile real-time measurement techniques and recent advancements in characterizing the ultrafast transient MDS dynamics of STML lasers, including spatial mode switching, optical rogue waves, mode-locking buildup process, three-dimensional soliton molecules, soliton explosions, and breathing multimode solitons. Finally, we outline some perspectives on how real-time measurement methods could advance the study of multidimensional soliton dynamics in STML in the near future.
tldr: This review surveys spatiotemporal mode-locking in multimode fiber lasers, focusing on multidimensional dissipative soliton dynamics revealed by real-time measurement techniques.
motivation: Spatiotemporal mode-locked fiber lasers provide a platform for nonlinear multidimensional physics and applications such as high-energy pulse generation and metrology, but understanding ultrashort pulse formation in nonlinear multimode resonators remains challenging.
method: The authors review the general principles of spatiotemporal mode-locking and summarize real-time measurement techniques used to characterize ultrafast transient dynamics of multidimensional dissipative solitons.
result: The review covers observed phenomena including spatial mode switching, optical rogue waves, mode-locking buildup, three-dimensional soliton molecules, soliton explosions, and breathing multimode solitons.
conclusion: The paper outlines perspectives on how real-time measurement methods could advance the study of multidimensional soliton dynamics in spatiotemporal mode-locked fiber lasers.

title: Force-decomposition Mechanotyping Reveals Capillary And Bulk-viscoelastic Regimes In Phase-separated Condensates
authors: Yongjie Guo, Pengcheng Nie, Boya Li, Yi Lin And Dongshi Guan
abstract: The mechanics of liquid-liquid phase-separated (LLPS) condensates are commonly interpreted using a capillary-fluid picture, in which droplet response is governed by interfacial tension and viscous dissipation. This framework explains many synthetic coacervates and simple phase-separated liquids, but its applicability to biomolecular condensates containing transient multivalent molecular networks remains uncertain. Here we introduce a long-needle atomic force microscopy platform for single-droplet force-decomposition mechanotyping. By probing individual microscale condensates with a vertically aligned glass fiber, the method separates interfacial contact-line forces, dynamic-meniscus dissipation and bulk mechanical resistance without assuming Newtonian fluid behavior or prescribing a constitutive model. We demonstrate that electrostatic polypeptide coacervates occupy a capillary-dominated regime, with tunable interfacial tension and shear-thinning rheology that can be precisely modulated by ionic strength. In contrast, the tested protein condensates, including Ataxin-2, occupy a bulk-viscoelastic regime, where the measured force grows with indentation and yields an apparent modulus that increases with loading rate. We further resolve the distinct relaxation dynamics that underpin these two mechanical regimes: the coacervates recover towards a capillary equilibrium through contact-line and dynamic-meniscus relaxation, whereas the protein condensates display an initial exponential relaxation followed by a long-time power-law decay, consistent with a broad spectrum of transient intermolecular bond lifetimes. Our results establish a quantitative framework for determining the dominant mechanical regime of LLPS condensates and provide a general strategy for investigating the mechanics of complex fluids and soft materials at the microscale.
tldr: A long-needle atomic force microscopy platform is used to mechanotype individual liquid-liquid phase-separated condensates, distinguishing capillary-dominated from bulk-viscoelastic mechanical regimes.
motivation: The standard capillary-fluid picture of condensate mechanics may fail for biomolecular condensates containing transient multivalent molecular networks, so a model-independent way to determine the dominant mechanical regime is needed.
method: Single microscale droplets are probed with a vertically aligned glass fiber (long-needle AFM), decomposing forces into interfacial contact-line, dynamic-meniscus dissipation, and bulk resistance without assuming Newtonian behavior or a constitutive model.
result: Electrostatic polypeptide coacervates are capillary-dominated with ion-tunable interfacial tension and shear thinning, whereas protein condensates such as Ataxin-2 are bulk-viscoelastic, showing rate-dependent apparent modulus and exponential-then-power-law relaxation.
conclusion: The work provides a quantitative framework for identifying the dominant mechanical regime of LLPS condensates and a general strategy for microscale mechanics of complex fluids.

conclusion: The review emphasizes the particle-physics structure of Higgs-R^2 inflation and its viability as a UV-complete inflationary framework.
